bib.title: Appendix. AI Systems Performance Checklist (175+ Items)
bib.venue: O'Reilly, AI Systems Performance Engineering (book appendix)

question: Which process-level and low-level practices should an AI systems performance engineer check when profiling and tuning training and inference on NVIDIA GPU systems?
contributions: A checklist of about 175+ tips in 18 categories, from tuning mindset and OS settings to CUDA, precision, networking, serving and power.

limits: Almost every number is an unsourced rule of thumb with no model, GPU, dataset or run count; the book's own conclusion says the list is not exhaustive and not every item applies.
The torch.compile gain is given as two different ranges (10%-40% and 20%-50%) in one item.
Hardware advice targets NVIDIA Grace Blackwell (GB200/GB300 NVL72) and mentions Vera Rubin; it will date as hardware changes.
Mostly training and cluster advice; inference items are two sections (Efficient Inference and Serving, Multinode Inference and Serving).
Item count: the title says 175+; the text states no exact count.
practices: Optimize the biggest runtime/cost contributor first and profile before and after every change (Mindset).
Pin versions and configs in source control and run performance regression benchmarks in CI (Reproducibility).
Match CPU cores (about one per GPU), DRAM and storage to GPU feed rates; keep tightly coupled jobs within one NVLink domain (System Architecture, Multi-GPU).

Pin processes to the local NUMA node, set THP to always or madvise (madvise if latency-critical and jittery), raise memlock, enable GPU persistence mode, keep driver/CUDA identical across nodes (OS and Driver).
Keep ECC on for data-center GPUs; use MPS/MIG to raise utilization of small jobs and keep persistence on with MIG (GPU Resource Management).
Use parallel data loaders, pinned memory, async transfers and fast NVMe/GDS to keep GPUs fed (I/O Optimization).
Use Nsight Systems/Compute, NVTX and DCGM to classify the job as compute, memory, I/O or network bound, and keep a regression benchmark set (Profiling).
Prefer BF16 over FP16, TF32 for easy FP32 speedups, FP8 first for inference and NVFP4 only after calibration (Arithmetic).
Use torch.compile (reduce-overhead mode), CUDA Graphs, fused kernels, FlashAttention and Triton for hotspots (CUDA tuning, Advanced Tuning).
For serving: continuous batching, specialized runtimes (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Dynamo), NIXL for KV transfer, KV offload, warm-up, tail-latency (p99) monitoring (Efficient Inference).
Disaggregate prefill and decode, shard oversized models by tensor/pipeline parallelism, offload memory for long contexts (Multinode Inference).
Monitor thermals (throttling near 85 C in some cases), test power limits with nvidia-smi -pl, and consolidate workloads onto busy GPUs (Power and Thermal).
